tldr: For every fixed hazard multiplier \(\theta>0\), the observed-data canonical gradient yields a sharp three-regime information phase diagram. Below one half, finite information is equivalent to \(E_P[S(1\mid X)^{-(1-2\theta)}]<\infty\); at \(\theta=1/2\), it is equivalent to \(E_P[\Lambda(1\mid X)]<\infty\); above one half, bounded outcomes and censoring positivity make the residual and treatment-martingale variances uniformly finite in the cumulative hazard. Under the power law near \(X=0\), the sub-half boundary is \(a(1-2\theta)<1\), with logarithmic failure at equality, whereas the half-multiplier boundary contribution is always integrable and only an interior cumulative-hazard singularity can destroy regularity. The nuisance-learning question is resolved negatively on the unchanged \(C^{20}\) class: unrestricted interior normalized-hazard complexity rules out the requested uniform cumulative-hazard learner, although the three prescribed arbitrary-zero-set profiles pass with exponents above one half. This learner no-go neither contradicts pointwise high-level results nor proves target-estimation impossibility. For the methotrexate multiplier \(\theta=0.2\), the boundary diagnostic is \(a<5/3\) together with the separate interior survival-moment check; the empirical tail and law-specific learner behavior remain unverified.
